settings.definition_quote: Throughout this paper we assume that the reward follows a Gaussian distribution, i.e., $\nu^{(i)}=\calN(\mu^{(i)},1)$... The entire time horizon $T$ is splitted into $M$ batches represented by a \emph{grid} $\calT=\{t_1,\cdots,t_M\}$... the policy $\pi_t$ depends only on observations up to time $t_{j-1}$.

tuning: static minimax grid t_m = floor(u_m), u_1 = a, u_m = a*sqrt(u_{m-1}), a = Theta(T^{1/(2-2^{1-M})})

source.label: thm.upper_bound_BaSE
source.quote: For $\gamma\ge 12$ and $\max_{i\in [K]}\Delta_i = O(\sqrt{K})$, we have $\bE[R_T(\pi^1_{\mathrm{BaSE}})] \leq C\log K\sqrt{\log(KT)}\cdot \sqrt{K}T^{\frac{1}{2-2^{1-M}}}$

results.notes: C is an unspecified numerical constant. Implies Theorem 1 (polylog version) and Corollary 1 (M=O(log log T) suffices for sqrt(KT) up to logs).

tuning: static geometric grid t'_m = floor(b^m), b = Theta(T^{1/M})

source.label: thm.upper_bound_BaSE
source.quote: $\bE[R_T(\pi^2_{\mathrm{BaSE}})] \leq C\log K\log (KT)\cdot  \frac{KT^{1/M}}{\min_{i\neq \star} \Delta_i}$, where $C>0$ is a numerical constant independent of $K, M$ and $T$.

results.notes: Implies Theorem 1 second bound and Corollary 1 (M=O(log T) suffices for K log T / Delta up to logs).

conditions: policies restricted to any static grid with M batches

source.label: thm.lower_bound
source.quote: For the $M$-batched $K$-armed bandit problem with time horizon $T$ and any static grid, the minimax and problem-dependent regrets can be lower bounded as $R_{\text{\rm min-max}}^\star(K,M,T) \ge c\cdot \sqrt{K}T^{\frac{1}{2-2^{1-M}}}$

results.notes: Minimax lower bound over static-grid batched policies; c numerical constant.

conditions: policies restricted to any static grid with M batches
R_pro-dep = inf_pi sup_{Delta>0} Delta * sup over instances with gaps in {0} U [Delta, sqrt(K)] of regret; bound holds for some (worst) Delta, not every Delta

source.label: thm.lower_bound
source.quote: $R_{\text{\rm pro-dep}}^\star(K,M,T) \ge c\cdot KT^{\frac{1}{M}}$, where $c>0$ is a numerical constant independent of $K,M,T$.

results.notes: Paper bounds Delta times worst-case regret over instances with minimum gap Delta, i.e. regret >= c K T^{1/M}/Delta for some Delta; expressed with Delta_min.

conditions: any M-batch policy, including adaptive (data-dependent, randomized) grids

source.label: thm.lower_bound_datadriven
source.quote: For the $M$-batched $K$-armed bandit problem with time horizon $T$ and any adaptive grid, the minimax and problem-dependent regrets can be lower bounded as $R_{\text{\rm min-max}}^\star(K,M,T) \ge cM^{-2}\cdot \sqrt{K}T^{\frac{1}{2-2^{1-M}}}$

results.notes: Proof gives c = 1/576. Implies Corollary 2 (M = Omega(log log T) necessary).

conditions: any M-batch policy, including adaptive grids

source.label: thm.lower_bound_datadriven
